The ZVCF is a **state evaluation**, not a trajectory held in equilibrium.
With $z=(q,\eta)$ and $v=\dot z$, evaluate $h_0(z)=h(z,0)$ while retaining
the declared deformation, parameters, other internal states, and contact mode.
For stationary constraints and the smooth mechanical model used here,

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{ZVCF}}:=-h_0(z),\qquad
a_{\mathrm{ZVCF}}=-M(z)^{-1}h_0(z).
$$ {#eq-zvcf_accel}

This uses the **signed drift-force** convention. Software that reports the
positive holding load instead returns $h_0$; label the sign explicitly.
In particular,

$$
\mathrm{ID}(z,0,0)=h_0(z),\qquad
\mathrm{ID}(z,0,a_{\mathrm{ZVCF}})=0.
$$ {#eq-zvcf_id}

Holding every coordinate of an underactuated model may require fictitious
actuators: $h_0$ need not lie in $\operatorname{range}(\bar B)$.
The formal holding load remains a useful diagnostic, not an executable policy.
For time-dependent constraints, zero velocity may be inadmissible; use a
constraint-consistent evaluation rather than silently resetting the state.

At the same configuration, define

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{vel.\,drift}}:=-[h(z,v)-h(z,0)],\qquad
\tau_{\text{drift}}=\tau_{\mathrm{ZVCF}}+
\tau_{\mathrm{vel.\,drift}}.
$$ {#eq-zvcf_split}

This difference contains every retained term that changes under the specified
velocity reset, including viscous damping. It is not generally a purely
inertial term. Velocity reset does not remove stiffness, stored elastic energy,
activation, or history encoded in retained internal states.

**Force evaluation does not identify stiffness.** Tangent stiffness is a
derivative of force with respect to displacement under stated loading and
boundary conditions. Material elasticity and geometric stiffness from
prestress can both contribute at zero velocity. For a beam under constant
tension $N>0$, the transverse restoring operator contains
$EI\,w_{ssss}-N\,w_{ss}$ even when $w_t=0$. Centrifugal loading is one possible
source of prestress; it is not the definition of geometric stiffness.
ZVCF subtraction is one reproducible way to partition loads. Direct evaluation
of the declared equation terms is another. Neither establishes material and
geometric stiffness separately without the tangent model.

The useful golf question is therefore precise: how much does a specified load
change when velocity is reset, and how sensitive is the answer to retained
shaft deformation, grip conditions, and contact? This exposes interactions
without calling a hypothetical frozen state a physically passive golfer.
